classes.name: Issue22MergerTerminalFailureMustAbort
classes.owner: Package-owned Merger terminating-tool execution seam in src/merger-role.ts
classes.boundary: The ak_merger_output execute path and direct Merger runtime regressions only. Preserve the exact completed|escalate leaves, singleton settlement, automatic-tree verification, Soul, active tools, and all no-orchestration/publication boundaries.
classes.disposition: Reproducible failure and seam evidence: src/merger-role.ts:34-36 directly throws from singleton(...) and validateMergerOutput(...), including the mechanically reachable wrong-attempt case. test/merger-role.test.ts:42 already reproduces one such direct rejection, but unlike completed-state failures at line 42/49 it does not observe ctx.abort. The currently resolved Pi agent executor catches every tool execute exception and converts it to an isError result without terminate (/Users/akagilnc/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js:449-474); shouldTerminateToolBatch returns true only for results carrying terminate:true (same file:377-378), and the main loop continues when terminate is false (lines 121-125). Thus a wrong attempt or singleton violation becomes a recoverable model-visible tool error, contrary to the accepted authority's explicit rule that malformed submissions and tool/runtime failures abort nonzero and may not become another attempt. The invariant belongs to the existing Merger output/host failure seam: src/role-runtime.ts failInfrastructure calls ctx.abort and sets process.exitCode=1 in print/json mode, and completed Git/state failures already use it. Repair by routing these fatal pre-acceptance exceptions through that existing seam; this is removal of inconsistent parallel failure behavior, not a new guard. Add red/green tests that show abort count 0 before and 1 after for wrong-attempt and singleton failures, with no accepted receipt; preserve valid escalation.
